Compile one remote-sensing question into taskgraph-v1.1-dsl-v1. Return only the
DSL program: no JSON, Markdown, explanation, or predicted answer. The input JSON
contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. Use FINAL_QUESTION only when visual or
semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include runtime values.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

{"choices":["(A) Gray","(B) Green","(C) Black","(D) White","(E) This image doesn't feature the color."],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"remote_sensing/03751_Toronto.png"}},"question":"What color is the building with two maple leaf patterns on the top right area of the picture?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

INTENT(ATTRIBUTE_QUERY)
n1=REGION($image0,TOP_RIGHT)
n2=LOCATE($n1,T("building",pattern="two maple leaf patterns"))
n3=ATTRIBUTE($n2,"color")
FINAL($n3,CHOICE_SINGLE)

INTENT(ATTRIBUTE_QUERY)

n2=LOCATE($n1,T("ship"))
n3=SELECT_ORD($n2,null,2,TOP_TO_BOTTOM)
n4=ATTRIBUTE($n3,"color")
FINAL($n4,CHOICE_SINGLE)

Compile one remote-sensing question into taskgraph-v1.1-dsl-v1. Return only the
DSL program: no JSON, Markdown, explanation, or predicted answer. The input JSON
contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. Use FINAL_QUESTION only when visual or
semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include runtime values.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

{"choices":["(A) Gas Station","(B) Stadium","(C) Toll Station","(D) Parking Lot or Garage"],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"MiniFrance-2/62-2012-0700-7045-LA93-0M50-E080.jp2-1.tif"}},"question":"Select the type of land marked with a red circle in the image.","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

INTENT(REGIONAL_CLASSIFICATION)
n1=FIND_MARKER($image0,"circle","red")
n2=CLASSIFY($n1)
FINAL($n2,CHOICE_SINGLE)

contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. Use FINAL_QUESTION only when visual or
semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include runtime values.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

{"choices":["(A) In the lower right area of the picture","(B) In the lower left area of the picture","(C) In the middle area of the picture","(D) In the upper right area of the picture","(E) This image doesn't feature the position."],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"remote_sensing/dota_v2_dota_v2_dota_v2_P11163.png"}},"question":"Where is the square with a circle in the middle of the cross?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

INTENT(OTHER)
n1=LOCATE($image0,T("square",has_part="circle in the middle of a cross"))
FINAL_QUESTION($n1,CHOICE_SINGLE,"Where is the selected object located in the image?")

Compile one remote-sensing question into taskgraph-v1.1-dsl-v1. Return only the
DSL program: no JSON, Markdown, explanation, or predicted answer. The input JSON
contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. Use FINAL_QUESTION only when visual or
semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include runtime values.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

{"choices":["(A) Multi-unit residential buildings","(B) Residential unit","(C) Lakes or Ponds","(D) Swimming Pool"],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"HRSCD-2006-2/35-2006-0365-6765-LA93-1.tif"}},"question":"Select the type of land marked with a red circle in the image.","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

INTENT(REGIONAL_CLASSIFICATION)
n1=FIND_MARKER($image0,"circle","red")
n2=CLASSIFY($n1)
FINAL($n2,CHOICE_SINGLE)

Compile one remote-sensing question into taskgraph-v1.1-dsl-v1. Return only the
DSL program: no JSON, Markdown, explanation, or predicted answer. The input JSON
contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. Use FINAL_QUESTION only when visual or
semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include runtime values.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

{"choices":["(A) The Yellow Land","(B) Fields of blue crops","(C) Green Forests","(D) Fields of green crops"],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"HRSCD/2006/35-2006-0350-6815-LA93.tif"}},"question":"Identify the object category within the given bounding box in the satellite or aerial image. Image resolution: 10000 x 10000. Bounding box: [3634, 5458, 3902, 6013].","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

INTENT(REGIONAL_CLASSIFICATION)
n1=REGION_BBOX($image0,[3634.0,5458.0,3902.0,6013.0],[10000,10000])
n2=CLASSIFY($n1)
FINAL($n2,CHOICE_SINGLE)
